How Many Days Is Each US Festival? A Length Guide to the Majors

By PLURGASM @plurgasm ⏱ 4 min read

One of the first questions anyone asks before pulling the trigger on a festival is simple: how many days is this thing? Two-day send or a four-day marathon changes everything: your PTO, your travel budget, how much kandi you need to make.

So here's a clean, scannable rundown of how long the major US festivals typically run, grouped by genre. Use it to plan, then lock in the details.

One important note: the lengths below are the typical format. Festivals shift dates and add or drop days year to year, so always confirm the current-year dates on the official site (or our calendar) before booking anything. A * marks events that have notably changed length or format recently.

EDM & Electronic Festivals

  • EDC Las Vegas: 3 days * (per weekend; expanding to two weekends and a 12-day "Dusk Till Dawn" run in 2027)
  • Ultra Music Festival (Miami): 3 days
  • Electric Forest: 4 days * (has alternated between one and two weekends over the years)
  • EDC Orlando: 3 days * (expanded from 2 days)
  • Lost Lands: 3 days * (often adds a Thursday pre-party; has steadily grown)
  • Lightning in a Bottle: 5 days (one of the longest in the US)
  • Bass Canyon: 3 days
  • North Coast (Chicago): 3 days
  • Imagine Music Festival: 3 days
  • Dancefestopia: 4 days
  • Wakaan Music Festival: 3 days
  • Elements Music & Arts Festival: 3 days
  • Dirtybird CampINN: 3 days
  • Okeechobee: 4 days
  • Sonic Bloom (CO): 4 days
  • Gem & Jam (AZ): 4 days
  • Beyond Wonderland at the Gorge: 2 days
  • Beyond Wonderland SoCal: 2 days
  • Project GLOW (DC): 2 days
  • Forbidden Kingdom: 2 days
  • Escape Halloween: 2 days
  • Hard Summer: 2 days
  • Nocturnal Wonderland: 2 days
  • Countdown NYE: 2 days
  • Dreamstate SoCal: 2 days
  • ARC Music Festival (Chicago): 3 days
  • CRSSD Festival (San Diego): 2 days
  • Sunset Music Festival (Tampa): 2 days
  • Decadence (CO / AZ, NYE): 2 days
  • Global Dance Festival: 2 days
  • Lights All Night: 2 days
  • Ubbi Dubbi: 2 days
  • Freaky Deaky: 2 days
  • Goldrush (AZ): 2 days
  • Phoenix Lights: 2 days
  • Same Same But Different: 3 days
  • Northern Nights: 3 days
  • Desert Hearts: 3 days
  • Infrasound (MN): 3 days
  • Breakaway Festival series (Ohio, Boston, Carolina, Nashville, and many more cities): typically 2 days each

Major Multi-Genre Festivals

  • Coachella: 3 days per weekend, across 2 weekends
  • Bonnaroo: 4 days * (taking 2027 off; plans to return in 2028)
  • Lollapalooza: 4 days * (grew from 3 days)
  • Austin City Limits: 3 days per weekend, across 2 weekends
  • Outside Lands: 3 days
  • Governors Ball: 3 days
  • Life Is Beautiful: 3 days * (has gone through format changes)
  • Hangout Music Festival: 3 days
  • Sea.Hear.Now: 2 days

Country Festivals

  • Country Thunder (Arizona & Wisconsin): 4 days
  • Stagecoach: 3 days
  • Watershed: 3 days
  • Tortuga Music Festival: 3 days
  • Faster Horses: 3 days

Rock / Alternative / Metal

  • Aftershock: 4 days
  • Sonic Temple: 4 days
  • Welcome to Rockville: 4 days
  • Louder Than Life: 4 days
  • Riot Fest: 3 days
  • Inkcarceration: 3 days

Jam / Camping Festivals

  • Hulaween: 4 days
  • Peach Music Festival: 4 days
  • High Sierra Music Festival: 4 days
  • Summer Camp Music Festival: historically 3 days * (cancelled for 2026)

The Longest US Festivals

If you want maximum days per trip, these go the longest: Lightning in a Bottle leads at 5 days, followed by a big cluster of 4-day events: Bonnaroo, Electric Forest, Country Thunder, Aftershock, Sonic Temple, Welcome to Rockville, Louder Than Life, Lollapalooza, Hulaween, Okeechobee, and more.

The short version

Most US festivals land at 2 or 3 days, the big destination camping events run 4, and a rare few stretch to 5. But the only number that actually matters is the one on this year's official lineup: formats change, weekends get added, and events get cancelled (RIP Summer Camp 2026). When in doubt, check the source before you book the flight.
